subject: math
title: 2D Shapes and 3D Objects: Name, Sort and Find Matching Halves
seo_title: Grade 1 Math 2D Shapes and 3D Objects Worksheets: Sorting Rules, Faces and Matching Halves (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Sort three-dimensional objects and two-dimensional shapes according to one attribute at a time, and identify the sorting rule being used
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on 2D shapes and 3D objects for the Ontario curriculum: name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles and hexagons, sort by one attribute and find the rule, name cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres, trace flat faces and find matching halves. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Look at one thing at a time: sides, corners, flat or curved. Turning never changes the name.
key_sub: A square on its corner is still a square. A ball is a sphere, not a circle. Trace a flat face of a 3D object to get a 2D shape. Matching halves land exactly on each other when you fold.

faq.q: What shapes do Grade 1 students learn in Ontario math?
faq.a: In Spatial Sense, Grade 1 students sort 2D shapes and 3D objects by one attribute at a time and name the sorting rule, find 2D shapes in 3D objects, and make shapes with matching halves. They name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles and hexagons, and cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders, cones and spheres.

faq.q: What is the difference between a 2D shape and a 3D object?
faq.a: A 2D shape is flat, like a drawing on paper. A 3D object is solid and you can hold it, like a ball (a sphere) or a soup can (a cylinder).

faq.q: What does “matching halves” mean in Grade 1?
faq.a: A shape has matching halves when you fold it on a line and the two halves land exactly on each other, like a heart or a butterfly. This is the start of learning about symmetry.

faq.q: How can I help my Grade 1 child learn shapes at home?
faq.a: Go on a shape hunt: find a ball (sphere), a soup can (cylinder), a cereal box (prism) and a number cube (cube). Trace their flat faces, sort the objects by what rolls, and fold paper cut-outs to look for matching halves.

sets.title: Sort by one attribute: find the rule

items.q: These are in one group. What is the sorting rule?
items.e: Some are squares and some are rectangles. Every shape has 4 sides. The rule is 4 sides.
Each one has a curved part. Each one can roll. The rule is they can roll.

items.q: How many squares can you see?

items.q: Ava uses the same 2 groups. Where does a circle go?
items.e: A circle has no straight sides. It does not go in either group.
A number cube has only flat faces. It slides. It does not roll.

items.q: These objects are in one group. What is the sorting rule?
items.e: None of them has a curved part. Every face is flat. The rule is only flat faces. Only the pyramid has a point.
